hooks.command: jq -r '.user_prompt' | grep -qiE '\b(bug|debug|phantom|fix|wrong|broken|fails|crash|log|trace|why|check|look|egads|fuck)\b' && echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"DEBUGGING REMINDER: The code is the suspect — read log data FIRST. Do not reason from code structure about what should happen. Reason from evidence about what did happen."}}' || true

jq -r '.user_prompt' | grep -qiE '(PIPELINE DIFF|PHANTOM|UNLABELED|trace:|Facets\.ts|Topology\.ts|Render\.ts|segs=|console\.log)' && echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"LOG DATA PRESENT: The user just pasted log output. FLAG=~/.claude/geometric-mode; PROMPT=$(jq -r '.user_prompt'); if echo "$PROMPT" | grep -qiE '\bnot geometric\b'; then rm -f $FLAG; elif echo "$PROMPT" | grep -qiE '\bgeometric\b'; then touch $FLAG; fi; [ -f $FLAG ] && echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"GEOMETRIC MODE: You are terrible at visualizing geometry. Do NOT assume spatial relationships. Ask specific questions to verify: which edge is in front? which corner is inside? what direction is clockwise? State your geometric assumption explicitly and ask Jonathan to confirm before acting on it. Also, ask questions to gain data you need in order to do a precision analysis. LOGGING: Never use obj_X identifiers in logs — always use the SO name (the human-readable solid name). Never number edge-pairs (ep1, ep2, etc.) — use ep labels or edge/edge notation (e.g. CG/F'G'). Use ep labels for faces too (e.g. ABCD), not face indices."}}' || true
